known.title: Keep turn locks from exhausting the application database pool
Replay the saved answer when a confirmation is repeated
Gate: Match the spend-cap proof to its actual test name

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Scale.
Case: normal use - ten people ask questions in different chats concurrently.
Each turn reserves a Prisma connection for the entire model run, while its callback uses the same Prisma pool for canStart, touch, tools and usage recording (assistant.turn.ts:121,133,175). The starter's libs/core/server/src/prisma/prisma.service.ts:9 supplies no pool override; [node-postgres defaults to ten connections](https://node-postgres.com/apis/pool). Ten running turns therefore occupy every connection while waiting for additional connections themselves. Answers and unrelated database-backed routes stall until transactions time out. Keep lock coordination from consuming the connections its callback requires.
Adds work: prevent pool starvation during turn locking; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Keep turn locks from exhausting the application database pool

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional.
Case: normal use - a client resends a confirmation after losing its response.
For confirmations, start is set to saved.length, so saved.slice(start + 1, ...) is always empty. A repeated confirmation consequently returns only done, losing the original text and data blocks even though the change succeeded. This breaks the API standard that a repeated action gives back its first result. Locate the saved confirmation receipt and replay its associated response without executing another change. The repeated-confirm test currently checks only write and model-call counts.
Adds work: replay the saved confirmation response; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Replay the saved answer when a confirmation is repeated

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3 (floor: agents)
Raise: Functional.
Case: normal use - a tool repeatedly returns an unavailable or invalid-input result.
Throwing here does not stop the agent: the prebuilt [ToolNode catches ordinary tool exceptions and returns error ToolMessages](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/main/libs/langgraph-core/src/prebuilt/tool_node.ts). The model can request the tool again, and callTool executes before this counter is checked again. Attempts therefore continue beyond the intended two-failure limit until the separate recursion limit intervenes. Enforce the stop at a boundary the tool error handler cannot swallow, as the agents skill's “Cap retries in code” Must rule requires.
Adds work: enforce the existing two-failure stop; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Agents: Cap retries in code

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test.
Case: normal use - CI runs test_5_a_used_up_cap_shows_one_line with FORGE_STARTER_LIVE=1.
This expected name ends with “other routes work”, but assistant-turn.e2e-spec.ts:546 names the case “other routes still work”. tests/test_starter_tree.py:326 checks for a contiguous substring, so the proof fails even when every API test passes. Make the expected name match the actual case.
